\chapter{Boolean Analysis --- Product Differentiation}
%%% generated by the blueprint pipeline from TCSlib.BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.ProductDifferentiation
\section{Overview}
Gaussian product densities and their first mean derivatives have common local integrable envelopes. Differentiation under the integral gives continuously differentiable bounded Gaussian averages and a uniform derivative norm bound.

\section{Declarations}

\begin{lemma}[Common Gaussian density and derivative envelope]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.gaussianPDFReal_two_derivatives_dominated}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.gaussianPDFReal_meanDerivative_dominated, BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.gaussianPDFReal_secondMeanDerivative_dominated, BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.hasDerivAt_gaussianPDFReal_mean}
\difficulty{5}
Let $v>0$ and $M\ge0$, and write $p_v(m,z)=(2\pi v)^{-1/2}\exp(-(z-m)^2/(2v))$. There is
a nonnegative Lebesgue-integrable function $b:\mathbb R\to\mathbb R$ such that for every
$m,z\in\mathbb R$ with $|m|\le M$, all three bounds hold:
\[p_v(m,z)\le b(z),\qquad \left|\frac{z-m}{v}p_v(m,z)\right|\le b(z),\qquad \left|\left(\frac{(z-m)^2}{v^2}-\frac1v\right)p_v(m,z)\right|\le b(z).\]
\end{lemma}

\begin{definition}[Mean derivative of a Gaussian product density]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.gaussianProductDensityDerivative}
\leanok
Let $I$ be finite and $v\ge0$. Write $p_v(c,z)$ for the $N(c,v)$ density when $v>0$ and set $p_0(c,z)=0$; define $G_v(c,z)=\prod_{i\in I}p_v(c_i,z_i)$ and interpret division by zero as zero. Let $A_v(c,z)$ be the linear functional $h\mapsto\sum_i\bigl(\prod_{j\ne i}p_v(c_j,z_j)\bigr)((z_i-c_i)/v)p_v(c_i,z_i)h_i$. The product-density derivative is $A_v(c,z)$ for mean and input vectors $c,z\in\mathbb R^I$.
\end{definition}

\begin{lemma}[Derivative as density times score]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.gaussianProductDensityDerivative_eq_density_smul_score}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.gaussianProductDensityDerivative}
\difficulty{4}
Let $I$ be a finite set, let $v\ge 0$, and let $c,z\in\mathbb R^I$. The derivative of
the product Gaussian density with respect to its mean, viewed as a linear functional on
$\mathbb R^I$, equals the product density multiplied by the linear functional
$h\mapsto\sum_{i\in I}((z_i-c_i)/v)h_i$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Derivative of a product Gaussian density]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.hasFDerivAt_gaussianProductDensity}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.gaussianProductDensityDerivative, BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.hasDerivAt_gaussianPDFReal_mean}
\difficulty{4}
Let $I$ be a finite index set, let $v\ge0$, and let $c,z\in\mathbb R^I$. The function
$m\mapsto\prod_{i\in I}p_v(m_i,z_i)$ is differentiable at $c$, with derivative the
linear functional $h\mapsto\sum_{i\in I}\bigl(\prod_{j\ne
i}p_v(c_j,z_j)\bigr)((z_i-c_i)/v)p_v(c_i,z_i)h_i$, where $p_v$ is the Gaussian density
of variance $v$ and division by zero is interpreted as zero.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Common envelope for density and derivative]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.gaussianProductDensity_derivative_dominated}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.gaussianPDFReal_two_derivatives_dominated, BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.gaussianProductDensityDerivative, BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.norm_coordinateProjection_le_one}
\difficulty{6}
Let $I$ be finite, let $v\ge0$ with $v\ne0$, and let $M\ge0$. There is a nonnegative
Lebesgue-integrable function $b:\mathbb R^I\to\mathbb R$ such that, for every
$m,z\in\mathbb R^I$ with $|m_i|\le M$ for all $i$, both the absolute value of the
product Gaussian density at $(m,z)$ and the operator norm of its mean derivative at
$(m,z)$ are at most $b(z)$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Joint continuity of the product density derivative]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.continuous_gaussianProductDensityDerivative_joint}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.gaussianProductDensityDerivative}
\difficulty{1}
Let $I$ be a finite set and let $v\ge 0$. The product Gaussian density derivative,
viewed as a continuous linear functional on $\mathbb R^I$, is jointly continuous as a
function of its mean vector $c\in\mathbb R^I$ and input vector $z\in\mathbb R^I$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Continuity of the product density derivative]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.continuous_gaussianProductDensityDerivative}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.gaussianProductDensityDerivative}
\difficulty{1}
Let $I$ be a finite set, let $v\ge 0$, and fix $c\in\mathbb R^I$. As a function of
$z\in\mathbb R^I$, the product Gaussian density derivative at mean $c$ and input $z$, as
a continuous linear functional on $\mathbb R^I$, is continuous in operator norm.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Integrability of the weighted Gaussian density derivative]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.integrable_gaussianProductDensityDerivative_smul}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.continuous_gaussianProductDensityDerivative, BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.gaussianProductDensityDerivative, BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.gaussianProductDensity_derivative_dominated}
\difficulty{4}
Let $I$ be a finite set, let $f:\mathbb R^I\to\mathbb R$ be measurable with $|f(z)|\le
1$ for every $z$, let $v>0$, and let $c\in\mathbb R^I$. Then the function sending $z$ to
$f(z)$ times the linear functional $h\mapsto\sum_{i\in I}\bigl(\prod_{j\ne
i}p_v(c_j,z_j)\bigr)((z_i-c_i)/v)p_v(c_i,z_i)h_i$ is integrable, as a function valued in
the continuous linear functionals on $\mathbb R^I$, with respect to Lebesgue measure on
$\mathbb R^I$. Here $p_v(m,t)$ is the density of the Gaussian with mean $m$ and variance
$v$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Coordinate bound in a maximum norm ball]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.abs_coordinate_le_of_mem_ball}
\leanok
\difficulty{4}
Let $I$ be a finite index set and let $c,m:I\to\mathbb R$. If $m$ lies in the open
metric ball of radius $\varepsilon$ about $c$ for the supremum norm, then $|m(i)|\le
\|c\|+\varepsilon$ for every $i\in I$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Derivative of a Gaussian product average]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.hasFDerivAt_integral_gaussianProductDensity}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.abs_coordinate_le_of_mem_ball, BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.continuous_gaussianProductDensityDerivative, BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.gaussianProductDensityDerivative, BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.gaussianProductDensity_derivative_dominated, BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.hasFDerivAt_gaussianProductDensity}
\difficulty{5}
Let $I$ be a finite set, let $v>0$, and let $f\colon\mathbb R^I\to\mathbb R$ be
measurable with $|f(z)|\le1$ for every $z$. The function $m\mapsto\int_{\mathbb R^I}
f(z)G_v(m,z)\,dz$, where $G_v$ is the product Gaussian density of variance $v$, is
Fréchet differentiable at every $c\in\mathbb R^I$, with derivative
$h\mapsto\int_{\mathbb R^I} f(z)A_v(c,z)[h]\,dz$, where $A_v$ is the mean derivative of
the product density.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Continuity of the integrated density derivative]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.continuous_integral_gaussianProductDensityDerivative}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.abs_coordinate_le_of_mem_ball, BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.continuous_gaussianProductDensityDerivative, BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.continuous_gaussianProductDensityDerivative_joint, BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.gaussianProductDensityDerivative, BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.gaussianProductDensity_derivative_dominated}
\difficulty{5}
Let $I$ be a finite set, let $f:\mathbb R^I\to\mathbb R$ be measurable with $|f(z)|\le
1$ for every $z$, and let $v>0$. The function of $c\in\mathbb R^I$ obtained by
integrating $f(z)$ times the product Gaussian density derivative at mean $c$ and input
$z$ with respect to Lebesgue measure is continuous as a map into the continuous linear
functionals on $\mathbb R^I$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Differentiability of product Gaussian averages]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.contDiff_one_integral_gaussianProductDensity}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.continuous_integral_gaussianProductDensityDerivative, BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.gaussianProductDensityDerivative, BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.hasFDerivAt_integral_gaussianProductDensity}
\difficulty{4}
Let $I$ be a finite set, and let $f:\mathbb R^I\to\mathbb R$ be measurable with
$|f(z)|\le 1$ for every $z\in\mathbb R^I$. For every variance $v>0$, the function
$m\mapsto\int_{\mathbb R^I}\left(\prod_{i\in I}p_v(m_i,z_i)\right)f(z)\,dz$ is
continuously differentiable, where $p_v(c,z)$ is the density at $z$ of the Gaussian
distribution with mean $c$ and variance $v$, and the integral is with respect to
Lebesgue measure.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Integral of the Gaussian product density derivative]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.integral_gaussianProductDensityDerivative_smul_eq_sum}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.gaussianCoordinate_first_kernel_integrable_bound, BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.gaussianProductDensityDerivative, BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.gaussianProductDensityDerivative_eq_density_smul_score, BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.integral_pi_gaussianReal_eq_integral_smul}
\difficulty{5}
Let $I$ be a finite index set, let $v>0$, let $c\in\mathbb R^I$, and let $f:\mathbb
R^I\to\mathbb R$ be measurable with $|f(z)|\le1$ for every $z$. Write $p_v(m,t)$ for the
density of the real Gaussian with mean $m$ and variance $v$, and let $Z$ have
independent coordinates with $Z_j\sim N(c_j,v)$. Then the integral, with respect to
Lebesgue measure on $\mathbb R^I$, of $f(z)$ times the linear functional
$h\mapsto\sum_{i\in I}\bigl(\prod_{j\ne
i}p_v(c_j,z_j)\bigr)\frac{z_i-c_i}{v}p_v(c_i,z_i)h_i$ equals the linear functional
$h\mapsto\sum_{i\in I}\mathbb E[\frac{Z_i-c_i}{v}f(Z)]h_i$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Bound for an integrated Gaussian density derivative]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.norm_integral_gaussianProductDensityDerivative_smul_le}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.gaussianCoordinate_first_kernel_integrable_bound, BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.gaussianProductDensityDerivative, BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.integral_gaussianProductDensityDerivative_smul_eq_sum, BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.norm_coordinateProjection_le_one}
\difficulty{4}
Let $I$ be a finite index set, and let $f:\mathbb R^I\to\mathbb R$ be measurable with
$|f(z)|\leq1$ for every $z$. Let $v\geq0$ with $v\ne0$, and let $c\in\mathbb R^I$. The
norm of the integral of $f(z)$ times the product Gaussian density derivative with mean
$c$ and variance $v$, integrated against Lebesgue measure on $\mathbb R^I$, is at most
\[
|I|\left(1+\frac1v\right).
\]
\end{lemma}
